independent_tests.scope: Pure local C-work byte, parser and mock contracts; no boot, network, CLI resume, registration or private preparation.

reviewed_guards: Default Python and PowerShell invocations are no-op. No reboot, registration, WSL, scientific execution or STOP-clear command exists in this helper.
Exact C deployment and non-reparse ancestry, dependency hashes, private manifest schema, explicit canonical thread UUID and original STOP SHA are checked before resume.
Launch requires both advanced LastBootUpTime and decreased GetTickCount64, plus a bounded first-two-hours new-boot handoff. These are launcher gates, not retrospective worker-terminal reconstruction.
CreateNew/fsync single-use consumption precedes network and Codex launch. Failure consumes the invocation, retains original artifacts and never automatically rearms.

Fresh public remote main must descend from the published anchor. Authority controls are read from that immutable commit; exact helper and launcher hashes must match current published bytes; main is rechecked after the snapshot.
Explicit thread resume uses stdin for the small source-controlled prompt, never --last. Thread identity, private manifest and CLI outputs remain in the explicitly private C namespace.
The newly launched Codex process birth and image are queried through its retained Popen handle and recorded. The launcher makes no CLI-terminal, descendant-closure or scientific-acceptance claim.
The prompt preserves old STOP authority and requires independent new-boot reconciliation and fresh scientific/runtime/resource/lock gates before subsequent work.
qualifications: No actual private handoff, boot query, remote authority fetch, Codex launch, registration or restart was performed by this reviewer.

Seven tests are source contracts, not proof of installed CLI resume behavior or successful post-boot execution. Python AST checks passed; PowerShell syntax parse is the producer's reported peer evidence.

Application network and boot-query bounds do not guarantee every kernel/filesystem/provider call returns within a hard wall-clock duration. Launched Codex intentionally has no finite computation timeout in this launch-only handoff.
If an exception occurs after Popen, failure evidence explicitly records an unproven created CLI and does not relaunch or claim it closed. This helper does not own or adopt scientific scopes.

Old worker terminal, historical clock continuity and job emptiness remain UNRECORDED. A new Windows boot is a separate aggregate reconciliation path requiring its own reviewed actual receipt; this source review cannot clear STOP.
